findings.title: XSS via unescaped request.referer in JavaScript context
findings.body: The referer is interpolated into a JavaScript string using ERB's `<%= %>` which only HTML-escapes. In Rails 3.2, `html_escape` does not escape single quotes. Since the value is placed inside a single-quoted JS string (`'<%= request.referer %>'`), an attacker who controls a page on the embeddable host can craft a URL containing a single quote to break out of the string and execute arbitrary JavaScript. For example, a referer like `http://embeddable-host.com/'); alert(document.cookie); ('` would pass the host check in `ensure_embeddable` but inject code. Use `j` (escape_javascript) helper or `raw json_escape` instead.

findings.title: URL interpolated into HTML attribute without escaping enables attribute injection
findings.body: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the URL is interpolated directly into an HTML anchor tag: `"#{url}"`. Although the URL is validated against `^https?\:\/\/`, it can still contain single quotes (e.g., `http://example.com/' onclick='alert(1)`). Since this content is stored with `cook_method: raw_html` (which returns raw as-is) and rendered with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in the embed view, this allows HTML attribute injection leading to XSS. The URL should be HTML-escaped before interpolation.

findings.title: NoMethodError when RSS item has no content element
findings.body: The line `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` will raise a NoMethodError if `i.content` is nil. Many RSS feeds use `<description>` instead of `<content:encoded>`, and SimpleRSS may return nil for `content` in such cases. This would crash the entire feed polling job, preventing any items from being imported. A nil check or fallback to `i.description` is needed.

findings.title: Non-atomic setnx + expire can permanently block URL retrieval
findings.body: The throttle mechanism uses two separate Redis commands: `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process crashes or is killed between these two calls, the key will exist without a TTL, permanently preventing retrieval of that embed URL. Use `$redis.set(retrieved_key, "1", ex: 60, nx: true)` (or the equivalent for the Redis version in use) to make this atomic.

findings.title: Origin check uses substring match instead of strict equality
findings.body: The postMessage origin validation uses `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` which checks if `e.origin` is a substring of `discourseUrl`. While not easily exploitable in most configurations, a strict equality check (`e.origin !== discourseUrl.replace(/\/$/, '')`) would be more robust. For example, if discourseUrl is `https://forum.example.com/` and a message arrives from origin `https://forum.example.com`, indexOf returns 0 (passes), but if discourseUrl were `https://forum.example.com.evil.com/`, a message from `https://forum.example.com` would also pass because it's a substring.

findings.title: Server-side request forgery via open-uri in import_remote
findings.body: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url).read` using open-uri, which follows redirects and can access internal network resources. While `TopicRetriever` validates the host against `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, `import_remote` is also called directly from the Disqus import task with arbitrary URLs from an XML file. If the initial URL redirects to an internal address (e.g., `http://169.254.169.254/` for cloud metadata), this could leak sensitive information. Consider using a restricted HTTP client that doesn't follow redirects to private IP ranges.

findings.title: Imported RSS content rendered without sanitization
findings.body: Posts imported via RSS use `cook_method: raw_html` which bypasses all Discourse sanitization (the `cook` method returns `raw` directly). The embed view then renders this with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. If an RSS feed contains malicious HTML (script tags, event handlers, etc.), it will be rendered as-is in the embed iframe. The content should be sanitized (e.g., using the `Sanitize` gem already in the Gemfile) before storage or before rendering.
